verses.text: After Jesus finished praying in one place, a disciple asked him, “Lord, teach us to pray, like John taught his disciples.”
Jesus said, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will happen on earth just as in heaven.”
“‘Give us the bread we need each day.”
“‘Forgive our sins, because we forgive everyone who owes us. Don’t bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.’”
Then he said, “Suppose you go to a friend’s house at midnight and say, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread.”
“‘A friend of mine just arrived after a long trip, and I have nothing to serve him.’”
“Suppose your friend calls from inside, ‘Don’t bother me. The door’s locked, and my children are in bed with me. I can’t get up and give you anything.’”
“I’m telling you, even if he won’t get up just because you’re friends, he’ll get up because you keep asking and give you whatever you need.”
“So keep asking, and you’ll receive. Keep searching, and you’ll find. Keep knocking, and the door will open for you.”
“Everyone who asks receives; everyone who searches finds; and the door opens for everyone who knocks.”
“Which father among you would hand his son a stone when he asks for bread? Or give him a snake when he asks for a fish?”
“Or if he asks for an egg, would you give him a scorpion?”
“Even you, with all your sin, know how to give good gifts to your children. How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!”
Jesus was driving out a demon that kept a man from speaking. When the demon left, the man spoke, and the crowd was amazed.
But some people said, “He drives out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
Others tested Jesus by demanding a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Every kingdom divided against itself falls apart, and a divided household collapses.”
“If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? You say I drive out demons by Beelzebul.”
“If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, then who do your people drive them out by? They’ll be your judges.”
“But if I drive out demons by God’s finger, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.”
“When a strong, armed man guards his own home, his possessions are safe.”
“But when someone stronger attacks and beats him, they take away the armor he trusted and divide up the goods.”
“Whoever isn’t with me is against me. Whoever doesn’t gather with me scatters.”
“When an unclean spirit leaves someone, it wanders through dry places looking for rest. When it can’t find any, it says, ‘I’ll go back to the home I left.’”
“When it returns, it finds the place swept clean and put in order.”
“Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself. They move in and settle there, and that person ends up worse than before.”
While Jesus was saying this, a woman in the crowd called out, “Blessed is the mother who gave birth to you and nursed you!”
But he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear God’s word and keep it.”
As the crowds kept gathering, Jesus began saying, “This generation is evil. It keeps demanding a sign, but no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah the prophet.”
“Just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.”

“The Queen of the South will stand up at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them. She came from far away to hear Solomon’s wisdom—and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.”
“The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it. They turned back to God when Jonah preached—and look, someone greater than Jonah is here.”
“Nobody lights a lamp and hides it in a cellar or under a basket. They put it on a stand so people coming in can see the light.”
“Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light. When it’s unhealthy, your body is full of darkness.”
“So check yourself: make sure the light you think you have isn’t actually darkness.”
“If your whole body is full of light, with no darkness in it, you’ll be completely lit up, like when a lamp shines its light on you.”
While Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited him to eat. Jesus went in and reclined at the table.
The Pharisee was surprised that Jesus didn’t first wash before the meal.
The Lord said to him, “You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and plate, but inside you’re full of greed and evil.”
“You fools! Didn’t the one who made the outside make the inside too?”
“Give to the needy out of what is within, and everything will be clean for you.”
“How terrible for you Pharisees! You carefully tithe mint, rue, and every herb, but you skip justice and love for God. You should’ve done those things without neglecting the others.”
“How terrible for you! You love the best seats in the synagogues and the respectful greetings in the marketplaces.”
“How terrible for you legal teachers and Pharisees—you hypocrites! You’re like hidden graves that people walk over without knowing.”
One of the legal experts said, “Teacher, when you say that, you’re insulting us too.”
Jesus said, “How terrible for you legal experts too! You pile heavy burdens on people, but you won’t lift even one finger to help them.”
“How terrible for you! You build tombs for the prophets, but your ancestors killed them.”
“So you’re witnesses who approve what your ancestors did: they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.”
“That’s why God’s wisdom said, ‘I’ll send them prophets and apostles. They’ll kill and persecute some of them,”
“‘so this generation will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets shed since the world began—”
“‘from Abel’s blood to Zechariah’s blood, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I’m telling you, this generation will be held responsible.”
“How terrible for you legal experts! You took away the key to knowledge. You didn’t go in yourselves, and you blocked the people who were trying to enter.”
When Jesus left, the legal teachers and Pharisees became furious and began pressing him with all kinds of questions,
lying in wait and trying to catch him saying something they could use to accuse him.
